nodes.name: Two-step Gradient Soaking
nodes.procedure: z-NiFe was synthesized via a two-step gradient soaking process at room temperature. The first gradient soaking process was conducted according to the published literature to prepare NiFe-LDH with good mechanical stability. In the second gradient soaking process, zwitterions (z-TCQ) were added to obtain a secondary hierarchical structure.

nodes.description: OER performance in a three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic performance of z-NiFe for OER was evaluated in 1 M KOH using a three-electrode system... z-NiFe required a lower overpotential (178 mV) to achieve a current density of 100 mAcm-2... at a high current density of 2000 mAcm-2, the overpotential of z-NiFe was only 195 mV... The Faradaic efficiency (FE) of z-NiFe during OER was close to 100% at 100 mAcm-2... z-NiFe demonstrated a lower Tafel slope of 28.5 mVdec-1... The corresponding KIE values are < 1.5 over the catalytic potential range (vs. Hg / HgO)

In the AEM-WE device... the z-NiFe-catalyzed AEM-WE device delivers an industrially required hydrogen production current density of 1000 mA cm-2 at a cell voltage of 1.76 V ... maintained stable operation for over 14000 h with a voltage degradation rate of 12.3 μV h-1

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS mapping confirm honeycomb structures and elemental distribution; TEM confirms interlayer spacing expansion consistent with XRD.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM) confirms that z-NiFe contains numerous honeycomb structures ... larger interlayer spacing (1.23 nm) than NiFe-LDH (1.07 nm), which is consistent with the TEM results

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows (001), (002), and (003) planes of Ni2Fe(SO4)0.5(OH)6(H2O)3.85; z-NiFe has a new peak at 7.14° indicating expanded interlayer spacing (1.23 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern, the crystallographic planes at (001), (002), and (003) are attributed to the refined Ni2Fe(SO4)0.5(OH)6(H2O)3.85 ... z-NiFe exhibits a new diffraction peak at 7.14°

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS shows a Ni:Fe atomic ratio of 1.25 for z-NiFe and lower dissolved metal ions compared to NiFe-LDH after stability tests.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-MS) reveals that the atomic ratio of Ni:Fe in the z-NiFe is approximately 1.25 ... z-NiFe exhibited a lower dissolved amount of Fe and Ni ions compared to NiFe-LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR shows peaks at 1385 and 1585 cm-1 for carboxylate groups (-COO-) and 3012 cm-1 for C-N+, indicating zwitterion coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectra ... arises absorption peaks of the carboxylate groups (-COO-) at approximately 1385 and 1585 cm-1 ... signal of C-N+ at 3012 cm-1 is present

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows z-NiFe maintains an alkaline surface microenvironment (CO3 2- > HCO3-) during OER, unlike NiFe-LDH which becomes acidic.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ Raman spectroscopy and OH- conductivity measurements reveal an alkaline-enriched surface environment ... peak area of CO3 2- consistently surpassed that of HCO3- with the voltage increase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge shift to lower energy indicates a reduced Fe valence state in z-NiFe compared to NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe K-edge to lower energy in z-NiFe, indicating a reduced Fe valence state compared to NiFe-LDH (Figure 1e).

properties.feature: Pre-edge peak and main absorption edge shift

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows negative shifts in Fe 2p and Ni 2p peaks for z-NiFe, confirming lower oxidation states, and presence of C-N bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS) of the Fe 2p and Ni 2p peaks in z-NiFe further demonstrates lower oxidation valence states ... signal of C-N bond is present in the N 1 s and C 1 s XPS spectra

nodes.characterization_summary: z-NiFe exhibits a more negative zeta potential (-23.64 mV) than NiFe-LDH (-16.45 mV) in 1 M KOH, indicating higher surface OH- concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: z-NiFe exhibited a more negative zeta potential (-23.64 mV) in 1 M KOH compared to NiFe-LDH (-16.45 mV) ... implied a higher concentration of OH- ions in the inner Helmholtz layer

nodes.evidence_snippet: OH- conductivity of z-NiFe as significantly higher than that of NiFe-LDH at various catalyst layer thicknesses, indicating that z-NiFe demonstrates a faster OH- transfer rate.
